alternate_names: Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy Kamakshi Tayee Ammavari Temple, Jonnawada

history.dynasty: Telugu Choda of Nellore region (Nellore district govt dates the temple to 1150 AD; legend credits King Manumasiddhi with building the shrine)
history.period: 12th century (1150 AD per Nellore district government)
history.summary: DUPLICATE RECORD: CSV row 30 ('Mallikarjuna Swamy Kamakshi Tai Temple, Nellore') refers to the same temple already covered by seq 27 — the Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy Kamakshi Tayee Ammavari Temple at Jonnawada village on the Penna river, about 12 km from Nellore city. Both CSV names name the same deity pair (Mallikarjuna Swamy + Kamakshi Tai) and all web sources (Nellore district govt, Tripadvisor) point to this single Jonnawada shrine. Recommend deleting or merging row 30 rather than treating it as a separate temple. Researched identically: the temple is tied in the Skanda Purana to sage Kashyapa's yagna at Rajathagiri (later Jonnawada), with Shiva emerging from the sacrificial kunda as a linga and Parvati self-manifesting as Kamakshi; Adi Shankaracharya is said to have installed a Sri Chakra yantra here. The district government records its construction in 1150 AD.

name: Mallikarjuna Swamy Kamakshi Tai Temple
town_description: Jonnawada (Jonnavada) is a village on the northern bank of the Penna river in Nellore district, about 12 km from Nellore city. It is a pilgrim centre built almost entirely around its Kamakshi-Mallikarjuna temple, with the sacred Kasyapa Theertham tank nearby; most visitors stay in Nellore and come for a day trip.

travel.airport: Tirupati International Airport, approx. 143 km (per Nellore district govt); taxis available.
travel.railway: Nellore Railway Station, approx. 15 km, well connected across India.
travel.road: Approx. 12 km from Nellore city; reachable by bus, auto and taxi from Nellore.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Dussehra and Vaisakha Brahmotsavams are the grandest times.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily approx. 5:00 AM to 1:00 PM and 4:30 PM to 9:15 PM (per Nellore district govt; verify on the day of visit).
